description: We're a creative team that loves building, experimenting, and learning together. With strong programming and research skills, we bring different perspectives to every part of our project. Everyone has their own strengths, and each person gets space to contribute and have fun. We communicate daily, stay organized, and aren't afraid to try something new or rethink an approach. Most importantly, we're here to challenge ourselves, enjoy the hackathon, and build something we're proud of.
summary: Not A Safe Atmosphere is a city-builder and resource-management game that challenges players to build and expand a sustainable human settlement on Mars. Starting with a small outpost, players must construct buildings, balance resource production and consumption, and make strategic decisions about when and how to expand them. Using real NASA research and data, the game introduces the scientific, logistical, and engineering challenges of establishing a human presence beyond Earth. It addresses the challenge by transforming complex space exploration concepts into an interactive experience where players learn through their decisions and their consequences. By demonstrating how limited resources, environmental conditions, and interconnected systems affect a settlement's survival, our project makes the challenge of future Mars missions more engaging, accessible, and understandable.
details: A game meant to put decision-making to the test, it is a tycoon builder where you expand and carefully manage your resources. It aims to teach the player how a real mission on Mars would require careful planning and a high level of adaptability. The project is divided into two main parts: A website to introduce the project, built with HTML, CSS, and JavaScript, which is being hosted on Render, and a Godot project embedded into the website, built using Godot's own engine and programming language. By gamifying complex decisions and management, it teaches kids 7-12 years old the constraints of a real mission without being overwhelming.
